overall: Atlanta is off to a warm start with temps already at 82.4°F by 9:50 AM under clear skies (CLR/SKC) and a brisk warming rate of +3.6°F/hr over the past two hours. A Heat Advisory is in effect for portions of Georgia with heat index values up to 107°F expected. Conditions are tracking on the warmer side of typical for this time of morning, with no cloud cover to inhibit solar heating.
forecast_obs_notes: The mesoscale models (ECMWF: 92.9°F, HRRR: 92.7°F, NBM: 91.3°F) cluster tightly around the NWS narrative of a 93°F high, while GFS is a notable warm outlier at 97.2°F that is likely inflating the D1_NOW distribution; the META fused model discounts the GFS outlier and leans meaningfully hotter than ECMWF/HRRR alone, placing 62.2% probability in the 94–95°F even bucket versus 27.9% in 92–93°F.
max_temp_prediction: With 82.4°F already logged before 10 AM and the afternoon peak still roughly 4.5–5 hours away (modeled around 14.7–16h ET), there is ample room to reach the low-to-mid 90s under full sun. The active even-bucket market shows 92–93°F as the modal bin at 38.1%, but the META model — the most reliable signal — strongly favors 94–95°F at 62.2%, suggesting the market may be slightly under-pricing the higher bucket. Weighting the META distribution, a best-estimate daily high near 93.5°F is reasonable, with meaningful upside risk toward 94–95°F if the afternoon heat builds as the GFS and META models imply.
